source_resources.title: nanoGPT: train.py pretraining loop
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT open source license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, and Day 46-48 Transformer model architecture.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Runnable pretraining scripts and step-by-step tensor mechanics are fully self-contained in the curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Heavy abstraction layer wrapping distributed training; nanoGPT exposes raw PyTorch loops without framework overhead.
High-performance enterprise distributed framework; unsuitable for local educational first-principles comprehension.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: train.py: get_batch(split): x = data[i:i+block_size], y = data[i+1:i+1+block_size]
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.

High-level API focus rather than building from raw tensor fundamentals.

source_resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
source_resources.author: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3.2.1: Scaled Dot-Product Attention equation and query/key/value matrix definitions
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference to open-access paper; all explanations and mathematical formulations in this curriculum are original works.
source_resources.prerequisites: Linear algebra, matrix multiplication, softmax probability distributions
source_resources.selection_rationale: The foundational primary literature establishing scaled dot-product attention, multi-head projection mechanisms, and autoregressive causal masking.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Open-access paper freely hosted on arXiv.org; no paywall.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete original algebraic derivations, matrix examples, variance proofs, and tensor diagrams are self-contained in the curriculum text without external document dependency.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Bahdanau et al.: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (ICLR 2015)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pioneered additive attention in RNNs, but Vaswani scaled dot-product attention replaced additive alignment in modern LLM architectures due to parallel matrix multiplication speed.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Shaw et al.: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations (NAACL 2018)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Introduces relative positional biases into attention; deferred to subsequent positional embedding modules after absolute scaled attention is thoroughly mastered.
Selected jointly as the primary code reference: translates Section 3.2 of the Vaswani paper into minimal, idiomatic PyTorch tensor operations.

source_resources.title: The Annotated Transformer
source_resources.author: v2022: Austin Huang, Suraj Subramanian, Jonathan Sum, Khalid Almubarak, Stella Biderman; original: Sasha Rush (Harvard NLP)
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: subsequent_mask implementation using torch.triu and triangular boolean masking
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT License terms; all text, examples, and exercise code in this curriculum are original works.
source_resources.prerequisites: Intermediate Python, PyTorch broadcasting and tensor slicing semantics
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely used pedagogical commentary that pairs every paragraph of the original Vaswani paper with an executable, testable code cell.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publicly hosted on Harvard SEAS and GitHub pages.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum provides standalone hand-worked numerical tables, explicit causal mask verification scripts, and offline analytical proofs.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Spectacular visual diagrams and intuitive color-coding, but lacks executable tensor code and formal numerical shape validation.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Stanford CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning (Lecture 10)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Rigorous academic slides and video lectures, but access to assignment grading is restricted to Stanford enrolled students.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Vaswani et al.: Attention Is All You Need
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: The original primary paper; Annotated Transformer annotates it directly.

source_resources.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
source_resources.author: Biao Zhang, Rico Sennrich (University of Edinburgh)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Variance, standard deviation, and LayerNorm basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary paper showing that mean-centering in LayerNorm can be discarded without performance loss, speeding up modern LLMs (LLaMA, Gemma).

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original LayerNorm formulation with mean-centering; RMSNorm is compared directly against it as an optimization.
Batch-dependent statistics; unsuitable for autoregressive sequence modeling.

source_resources.safe_fallback: RMSNorm formulas and numerical comparisons are derived completely in the lesson.
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4 RMSNorm (Equation 4) and Section 4.1 Invariance Analysis

source_resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
source_resources.author: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation and reference under arXiv open access terms; no paper figures or prose reproduced.
source_resources.prerequisites: Matrix multiplication and basic neural network concepts from Days 22-24 and 34-36.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational primary literature defining the Transformer architecture, multi-head attention, and scaled dot-product attention.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely hosted on arXiv.org; PDF and HTML available.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All mathematical formulas and structural definitions are self-contained in the lesson text.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: High-level visual intuition, but Vaswani et al. provides the primary mathematical specifications needed for implementation.
Co-primary: PyTorch line-by-line implementation alongside the paper equations.
